title: Separating Fact from Fiction: AI Does Not Set Prices at McDonald’s

reading.body:
This is a dispute about what a deployed system does, not a documented account of it doing something. The record here consists of a class action complaint and a company statement denying the central claim, and the complaint itself is not readable in the material provided. So the failure mode cannot be named from these facts. Whether any AI system set, recommended or influenced menu prices is not established.

What is established is narrower. A class action was filed alleging AI-powered menu price-fixing, three outlets reported on it, and the company published a response titled "Separating Fact from Fiction: AI Does Not Set Prices at McDonald's." That is a claim and a denial, not a finding. The location of any failure within a deployment, and the human check that might have caught it, cannot be identified without the complaint's text.

Catching a pricing failure of this kind would require access to the system's actual inputs and outputs, its role in the pricing process, and the records showing who approved each price. None of that is in the material. A lawsuit is not a verdict, and a company's denial is not proof either.
